title: Shipment record
html:
At 20:35:12, during the speeches, workstation WS-02 changed the shipment record of crate CR-017. You saw it in the system log: modify_manifest. What did it change?

That record is not in your files. It lives in the museum's collection system, behind an API: an address that returns data instead of a page.

Documentation: [[api]]

Example, the shipment of the other crate in the corridor:

[[api]]shipments/CR-012.json

Change the address to ask for the crate under the cloth.

prev_card.title: You caught the wrong clock
prev_card.html:
Corrected by 7 minutes, the covered crate passed at 20:47:08, ten seconds after Julien Moreau's badge opened the corridor door (20:46:58). Not Thomas Lefebvre. And CAM-04 recorded nothing from 20:41:08 to 20:58:40: WS-02 had switched it off.

The data term: Data quality

Data quality is how far you can trust data. The stills were real, but their times were 7 minutes off, and that pointed at the wrong person. The correction was one sentence in an unstructured report. Before you combine two sources, check that they use the same clock.

At what time did the crate leave the building?

hints: In the address bar, replace CR-012 with the crate ID from the trolley in stage 4.

In the record, original_destination is where the crate was supposed to go and current_destination where it goes now. The events list shows every change, oldest first: look for the status departed. The documentation page says what each D-code means.
D-01, conservation storage. D-03, the external loading dock. It left at 20:52:10.
